title: Fourth-derivative invariance bound
statement:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$ be a multilinear coefficient family on $n$ coordinates of degree at most $k$. Suppose the $2n$ real random variables $Z_{L,i},Z_{R,i}$ are mutually independent and each satisfies the invariance moment conditions: its mean and third moment are zero, its second moment is one, and its fourth moment is at most $9$, with finite fourth moment. If $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$ and $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}|$ everywhere, then
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(Z_L))-\mathbb E_\mu\psi(F(Z_R))\right|\le \frac C{12}\,9^k\sum_{i=1}^n \mathrm{Inf}_i[F]^2,
\]
where $F(Z)(\omega)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}Z_i(\omega)$ and $\mathrm{Inf}_i[F]$ is the influence of the Walsh-basis function defined by the same coefficients.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a multilinear coefficient family of degree at most $k$
The $2n$ random variables indexed by the two coordinate copies are mutually independent
Each random variable satisfies the invariance moment conditions
The absolute value of the fourth derivative of $\psi$ is bounded everywhere by $C$
replaced: Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ be a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$; let $I_i(F)=\sum_{S\ni i}a_S^2$. Let $(Z_{L,i},Z_{R,i})_{i=1}^n$ be a mutually independent family of $2n$ real inputs on a probability space, each measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. If $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$ and $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}|$ everywhere, then $|\mathbb E\psi(F(Z_L))-\mathbb E\psi(F(Z_R))|\le(C/12)9^k\sum_i I_i(F)^2$.
